correctness.rationale: Support invariance is verified by formula-structural induction for equality-free monadic language. Disjoint-union support equals the union of supports; finite C makes binary and arbitrary union closure equivalent. Finite join-irreducibles generate each union-closed family and are mandatory in any basis. The displayed outer-universal formula is true exactly on the family, on all nonempty structures including infinite. The finite violation bound follows from one element per colour; rank-two syntax bound and within-syntax rank-one counterexample are exact. Independent finite checker exhausts the support families through four colours; no extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The main 2026 paper Section 3.4 and the 2021 monadic type-normal-form full article were materially read and logically compared, not merely searched by title. The existing monadic realised-colour normal form is credited fully; the explicit equivalence of disjoint-union closure with the new restricted outer-universal rank-two grammar and canonical irreducible basis is not stated in those sources, although it follows by a short finite semilattice argument. Genuine published-finding corpus searches retrieved no equivalent finding; the strongest nearby items concern a different team-semantics union property. Scientific novelty is restricted and older indirect subsumption remains possible.
residual_risks: The novel theorem is structurally close to a short consequence of an established monadic basic form; prior priority may be limited, and an unlocated dedicated monadic disjoint-union preservation theorem could subsume it.
The published-finding corpus database is a nonexhaustive semantic index; negative search is not proof of unique priority.
Other older literature on monadic preservation was not exhaustively inspected.
Only finite supporting computations were run; all-domain correctness rests on the written induction, not the computation.

value.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly asks whether a restricted disjoint-union normal form survives without equality. A full, effective positive solution for a mathematically natural maximal purely unary sublanguage, together with a unique basis, a formula-independent rank bound in the requested syntax, and finite countermodel bounds, isolates a sharp tractable part of that question. This is more than a single example or arbitrary finite count, while the stronger general equality-free problem is left untouched. The derivation is elementary and known monadic support-normal-form foundations are acknowledged.
